questions.questionTextHi: बल देकर कहना
optionsEn: : Under Article 368, the Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution. Reason (R) : The Parliament is the Supreme Legislative body elected by the People of India. Code : (a) Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
optionsHi: : अनुच्छेद 368 के तहत संसद संविधान के किसी भी भाग में संशोधन कर सकती है। कारण (आर): संसद भारत के लोगों द्वारा निर्वाचित सर्वोच्च विधायी निकाय है। कोड: (ए) दोनों (ए) और (आर) सही हैं, और (आर) (ए) का सही स्पष्टीकरण है।
(ए) और (आर) दोनों सही हैं, लेकिन (आर) (ए) का सही स्पष्टीकरण नहीं है।
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). Article 368 of the Constitution of India, deals with the power of Parliament to amend the Constitution. Therefore, it says that notwithstanding anything in this Constitution, Parliament may in the exercise of its constitutional power amend by way of addition, variation or repeal, any provision of this Constitution in accordance with the procedure laid down in this Article. However, the Parliament cannot amend those provisions that form the 'basic structure' of the Constitution. This was ruled by Supreme Court in the Kesvananda Bharati Case (1973). The Parliament is the supreme Legislative Body elected by the People of India. Therefore Parliament has the authority to amend the Constitution. Thus, both assertion (A) and Reason (R) are individually correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.questionTextEn: Minimum how many times the Parliament has to meet in a year:
questions.questionTextHi: एक वर्ष में संसद की न्यूनतम कितनी बार बैठक होनी है:
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (B). Article 85(1) imposes a duty upon the President to summon each House of Parliament at such interval that six months shall not intervene between its last sitting in one session and the date appointed for its ﬁ rst sitting in the next session. So the Parliament must meet at least twice in a year.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (B) Article 85(1) imposes a duty upon the President to summon each House of Parliament at such interval that six months shall not intervene between its last sitting in one session and the date appointed for its ﬁ rst sitting in the next session. So the Parliament must meet at least twice in a year.

questions.questionTextEn: Consider the table given below : Parliament (Council of States) (House of the People) Not more than Not more than 552 250 members members and 12 nominated not more than 530 not more than 238 representatives of representatives of States plus not more States and Union than 2 nominated Territories Anglo-Indians and X. Which one of the following will ﬁ t in the place marked ‘X’?
questions.questionTextHi: नीचे दी गई तालिका पर विचार करें: संसद (राज्यों की परिषद) (लोगों का सदन) 552 से अधिक नहीं, 250 सदस्य और 12 मनोनीत, 530 से अधिक नहीं, 530 से अधिक नहीं, राज्यों के प्रतिनिधियों के 238 से अधिक नहीं, साथ ही राज्यों और संघ के 2 नामांकित प्रदेशों से अधिक नहीं, एंग्लो-इंडियन और एक्स। निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा 'X' चिह्नित स्थान पर फिट होगा?
optionsEn: Ministers who are not members of Parliament but who have to get themselves elected to either House of Parliament within six months after assuming oﬃ ce
Not more than 20 representatives of Union Territories
The Attorney General who has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of either House of Parliament
optionsHi: वे मंत्री जो संसद के सदस्य नहीं हैं, लेकिन जिन्हें पद ग्रहण करने के बाद छह महीने के भीतर संसद के किसी भी सदन के लिए निर्वाचित होना पड़ता है
केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों के 20 से अधिक प्रतिनिधि नहीं
अटॉर्नी जनरल जिसे संसद के किसी भी सदन की कार्यवाही में बोलने और भाग लेने का अधिकार है
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (C). The Parliament of India consists of (1) President (2) Lok Sabha (3) Rajya Sabha. The House of People shall consist of– (a) Not more than 530 representatives of States [Art. 81(1) (a)] chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies in the state. (b) Not more than 20 representatives of Union Territories [Art. 81(1)(b)]; (c) President, if he is of opinion that the Anglo-Indian Community is not adequately represented in the House of the People, could nominate not more than two members of that community to the House of the people. Note - It is noteworthy that the arrangements of the nomination of Anglo-Indian community in the Lok Sabha have not been extended beyond the stipulated date (25 January, 2020) by 'The Constitution (One hundred and Fourth Amendment) Act, 2019. Thus, in question 'X' stands for 20 representatives of UTs. So option (c) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following are/is stated in the Constitution of India? 1. The President shall not be a member of either House of Parliament. 2. The Parliament shall consist of the President and the two Houses. Choose the correct answer from the codes given below:
questions.questionTextHi: निम्नलिखित में से क्या भारत के संविधान में वर्णित है/हैं? 1. राष्ट्रपति संसद के किसी भी सदन का सदस्य नहीं होगा। 2. संसद राष्ट्रपति और दोनों सदनों से मिलकर बनेगी। नीचे दिए गए कोड से सही उत्तर चुनें:
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (B). Article 59 (1) of the Indian Constitution says that the President shall not be a member of either House of Parliament and Article 79 says that Parliament of Union shall consists of President and two Houses. So both the statement are correct.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (B) Article 59 (1) of the Indian Constitution says that the President shall not be a member of either House of Parliament and Article 79 says that Parliament of Union shall consists of President and two Houses. So both the statement are correct.

optionsEn: Elected members of the Lower House of the Parliament
Elected members of the Upper House of the Parliament
Elected members of the Upper House of the state Legislature
Elected members of the Lower House of the state Legislature
optionsHi: संसद के निचले सदन के निर्वाचित सदस्य
संसद के उच्च सदन के निर्वाचित सदस्य

optionsEn: Only the Rajya Sabha and not the Lok Sabha can have nominated members
There is a Constitutional provision for nominating two members belonging to the Anglo-Indian community to the Rajya Sabha
There is no Constitutional bar for nominated members to be appointed as a Union Minister
A nominated member can vote both in the Presidential
optionsHi: केवल राज्यसभा में ही मनोनीत सदस्य हो सकते हैं, लोकसभा में नहीं
राज्यसभा में एंग्लो-इंडियन समुदाय के दो सदस्यों को मनोनीत करने का संवैधानिक प्रावधान है
मनोनीत सदस्यों को केंद्रीय मंत्री नियुक्त किये जाने पर कोई संवैधानिक रोक नहीं है
एक मनोनीत सदस्य राष्ट्रपति पद के लिए दोनों मतदान कर सकता है
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). & (c) Both Houses of Parliament had nominated members. 12 in Rajya Sabha and 2 in Lok Sabha (Anglo-Indian Community). Under the amendment to Article -334 by 'The Constitution (One hundred and Fourth Amendment) Act, 2019 the arrangements of nomination for the representation of Anglo- Indian community in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies have not been extended beyond the stipulated date (25 January, 2020). Therefore, the arrangements of nominating Anglo-Indian members in the Lok Sabha has ended. Article 54 states that election of the President shall be done by an Electoral College consisting of the elected members of both the Houses of the Parliament and Legislative Assembly of the State. Thus nominated members are not eligible to vote for the election of President, but there is no bar for nominated member to be appointed as minister. He must be a member of Parliament or must become a member within six months after appointment as a Minister.

questions.questionTextEn: Who can legislate on the subjects which are not included in any of the lists of subjects given in the Constitution?
questions.questionTextHi: उन विषयों पर कौन कानून बना सकता है जो संविधान में दी गई किसी भी विषय सूची में शामिल नहीं हैं?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (B). Article 248 of Indian Constitution provides residual legislative powers to the Parliament. According to Article 248, the Parliament has exclusive power to make any law on any matter not enumerated in State or Concurrent List.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (B) Article 248 of Indian Constitution provides residual legislative powers to the Parliament. According to Article 248, the Parliament has exclusive power to make any law on any matter not enumerated in State or Concurrent List.

questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following statement is correct?
questions.questionTextHi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सही है?
optionsEn: All the members of Council of States are elected by State Legislative Assemblies.
As the Vice-President is the ex-oﬃ cio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, only a member of the Rajya Sabha can contest for the oﬃ ce of the Vice-President.

A point diﬀ erence between the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha is that while a candidate to Lok Sabha can contest from any State in India, a candidate to the Rajya Sabha should ordinarily be a resident of the State from where he is contesting.
The Constitution of India explicitly prohibits the appointment of a nominated member of the Rajya Sabha to the post of minister.
optionsHi: राज्य परिषद के सभी सदस्य राज्य विधान सभाओं द्वारा चुने जाते हैं।
चूंकि उपराष्ट्रपति राज्य सभा का पदेन सभापति होता है, इसलिए केवल राज्य सभा का सदस्य ही उपराष्ट्रपति पद के लिए चुनाव लड़ सकता है।

लोकसभा और राज्यसभा के बीच एक अंतर यह है कि जहां लोकसभा का उम्मीदवार भारत के किसी भी राज्य से चुनाव लड़ सकता है, वहीं राज्यसभा के लिए उम्मीदवार को आम तौर पर उस राज्य का निवासी होना चाहिए जहां से वह चुनाव लड़ रहा है।
भारत का संविधान स्पष्ट रूप से राज्य सभा के मनोनीत सदस्य की मंत्री पद पर नियुक्ति पर रोक लगाता है।
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). According to the then provision, option (c) was correct and the other options are wrong. Note: People’s Representative Act, 1951 was amended, in the year 2003, so the situation has changed now. The requirement that a candidate contesting an election to the Rajya Sabha from a particular State should be a voter in that particular State has been removed. Supreme Court in 2006 upheld the Constitutional validity of this Amendment.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (A) According to the then provision, option (c) was correct and the other options are wrong. Supreme Court in 2006 upheld the Constitutional validity of this Amendment.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following procedures will enable the adoption of a Money Bill that was once passed by the Lok Sabha but was amended by the Rajya Sabha?
questions.questionTextHi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी प्रक्रिया उस धन विधेयक को अपनाने में सक्षम बनाएगी जो एक बार लोकसभा द्वारा पारित कर दिया गया था लेकिन राज्यसभा द्वारा संशोधित किया गया था?
optionsEn: It will go to the President.
The Lok Sabha will have to pass it with 2/3rd majority of the members sitting and voting.
A Joint session of the two Houses will be called.
It will be deemed to have been passed if the Lok Sabha passes it again either by accepting or rejecting the amendments.
optionsHi: लोकसभा को इसे बैठने और मतदान करने वाले सदस्यों के दो-तिहाई बहुमत से पारित करना होगा।
दोनों सदनों का संयुक्त सत्र बुलाया जाएगा.
यदि लोकसभा संशोधनों को स्वीकार या अस्वीकार करके इसे दोबारा पारित कर देती है तो इसे पारित माना जाएगा।
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (D). According to Article 109, Lok Sabha has been given special powers regarding Money Bill. Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha. It can be detained by Rajya Sabha for a maximum period of 14 days and cannot be amended or rejected by Rajya Sabha. The Money Bill returned by Rajya Sabha with or without recommendation, may be accepted or rejected by Lok Sabha.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (D) According to Article 109, Lok Sabha has been given special powers regarding Money Bill. Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha. It can be detained by Rajya Sabha for a maximum period of 14 days and cannot be amended or rejected by Rajya Sabha. The Money Bill returned by Rajya Sabha with or without recommendation, may be accepted or rejected by Lok Sabha.

questions.questionTextHi: अध्यक्ष सदन के किसी सदस्य को बोलना बंद करने के लिए कह सकता है और दूसरे सदस्य को बोलने दे सकता है। इस घटना को इस रूप में जाना जाता है:
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (D). To maintain the highest tradition of Parliamentary System and proper functioning of Parliamentary Democracy, it is essential for the members of Parliament to observe a certain standard of conduct, both inside the House as well as outside the house. Their behaviour should be such as to enhance the dignity of Parliament and its members in general. Phenomenon given in options are described as under– 1. While the House is sitting, every member should enter and leave the chamber with decorum and in such a manner as not disturb the proceedings of the House. 2. A member is not to “cross the ﬂ oor,” i.e. pass between the chair and another member while the latter is speaking. A member is not to leave the chamber when the Speaker is addressing the House. Every member has to resume his seat as soon as the Speaker rises to speak or calls out ‘order’. 3. Interpellation is a Parliamentary procedure of demanding that a Government oﬃ cial explains some Act or policy. 4. The speaker can stop a member of Parliament from speaking and let another member speak. This phenomenon is known as yielding the ﬂ oor.

questions.questionTextEn: ‘Zero Hour’ is the contribution of which country to the Parliamentary System?
questions.questionTextHi: 'शून्यकाल' संसदीय प्रणाली में किस देश की देन है?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). ‘Zero Hour’ is an Indian innovation in the field of Parliamentary procedure. The emergence of zero hour can be traced to early sixties when many issues of great public importance and urgency began to be raised by members immediately after Question Hour, sometimes with prior permission of the chairman or some other times without such permission. Presently in Lok Sabha it is usually from 12:00 noon to 1:00 pm (after the question hour), while in Rajya Sabha it is 11:00 am to 12:00 noon (before the question hour). It is notable that the timing of question hour in Lok Sabha is 11:00 am to 12:00 noon, while in Rajya Sabha (from 2014) it is 12:00 noon to 1:00 pm.

questions.questionTextHi: लोकसभा में नियम, प्रक्रिया और कार्य संचालन के नियम 377 के तहत, लोकसभा सदस्यों द्वारा एक दिन में उठाए जा सकने वाले मामलों की अधिकतम संख्या है
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). Matters which are not point of orders or which cannot be raised under the rules relating to Questions, short Notice Questions, calling Attention, Motions etc can be raised under rule 377. Notice for raising a matter under rule 377 is to be given in writing addressed to the Secretary - General specifying clearly the text of the matter to be raised. No matter can be raised until the speaker has given his/her consent. As per the decision taken at a meeting of the speaker with Leaders of Parties. In 2015, the number of matters to be raised under Rule 377 has been increased from 20 to 30 per day to enable more members to raise their issues.

optionsEn: With the consent of all the states
With the consent of the majority of states
With the consent of the states concerned

optionsHi: बिना किसी राज्य की सहमति के
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (D). questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following statements is correct?
questions.questionTextHi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सही है?
optionsEn: A Money Bill is introduced in the Rajya Sabha.
A Money Bill can be introduced in either of the two Houses of the Parliament.
A Money Bill cannot be introduced in the Lok Sabha.
A Money Bill is introduced in the Lok Sabha.
optionsHi: धन विधेयक राज्य सभा में पेश किया जाता है।
धन विधेयक संसद के दोनों सदनों में से किसी एक में पेश किया जा सकता है।
धन विधेयक लोकसभा में पेश नहीं किया जा सकता।
लोकसभा में धन विधेयक पेश किया जाता है।
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (D). A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha. If any question arises whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not, the decision of the Speaker thereon is ﬁ nal. The Speaker is under no obligation to consult anyone. A Money Bill cannot be referred to a joint session of the Parliament. Rajya Sabha is required to return Money Bill within a period of 14 days from the date of its receipt. Thus, Rajya Sabha may withhold the bill maximum for 14 days [Art. 109(2)].

questions.questionTextHi: संसद के दोनों सदनों के संयुक्त सत्र की अध्यक्षता कौन करता है?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). Article 118 of the Constitution of India is related to the Rule of Procedure. Joint session of two Houses is presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. During the absence of the Speaker from any joint sitting, it is presided over by the Deputy Speaker of the House or if he is also absent, the Deputy Chairman of the Council of States and if he is also absent such other person as may be determined by the members present at a sitting, shall preside.

questions.questionTextEn: Consider the following statements: 1. The joint sitting of both Houses of the Parliament in India is sanctioned under Article 108 of the Constitution 2. The ﬁ rst joint sitting of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha was held in the year 1961 3. The second joint sitting of both Houses of Indian Parliament was held to pass the Banking Service Commission (Repeal), Bill Which of these statements is/are correct?
questions.questionTextHi: निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें: 1. भारत में संसद के दोनों सदनों की संयुक्त बैठक को संविधान के अनुच्छेद 108 के तहत मंजूरी दी गई है 2. लोकसभा और राज्यसभा की पहली संयुक्त बैठक वर्ष 1961 में आयोजित की गई थी 3. भारतीय संसद के दोनों सदनों की दूसरी संयुक्त बैठक बैंकिंग सेवा आयोग (निरसन), विधेयक को पारित करने के लिए आयोजित की गई थी इनमें से कौन सा कथन सही है/हैं?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (D). The joint sitting of both the Houses of Parliament in India is mentioned under Article 108 of the Constitution of India. The ﬁ rst joint session took place in 1961 to resolve the issue on the ‘Dowry Prohibition Bill,’ on which both the Houses had ﬁ nally agreed. The second joint session took place in 1978 on the Banking Service Commission (Repeal) Bill of 1977. The third joint session of the Parliament was held in March 2002 for Anti-Terrorism Bill (POTA).
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (D) The joint sitting of both the Houses of Parliament in India is mentioned under Article 108 of the Constitution of India. The ﬁ rst joint session took place in 1961 to resolve the issue on the ‘Dowry Prohibition Bill,’ on which both the Houses had ﬁ nally agreed. The second joint session took place in 1978 on the Banking Service Commission (Repeal) Bill of 1977. The third joint session of the Parliament was held in March 2002 for Anti-Terrorism Bill (POTA).

questions.questionTextEn: A deadlock between the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha calls for a joint sitting of the Parliament during the passage of 1. Ordinary Legislation 2. Money Bill 3. Constitution Amendment Bill Select the correct answer using the codes given below
questions.questionTextHi: लोकसभा और राज्यसभा के बीच गतिरोध के कारण 1. साधारण विधान 2. धन विधेयक 3. संविधान संशोधन विधेयक के पारित होने के दौरान संसद की संयुक्त बैठक बुलानी पड़ती है। नीचे दिए गए कोड का उपयोग करके सही उत्तर चुनें।
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). Article 108 of the Constitution of India deals with the joint sitting of both the Houses of the Parliament to resolve the deadlock between them. Joint sitting related to Money Bill is not required as Rajya Sabha has no power to block the passage and has to return the Bill within 14 days from the date of receipt. A Constitution Amendment Bill has to be passed by each House as prescribed in Article 368 of the Constitution. Thus, joint sitting is applicable in the case of ordinary Bill. So, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.questionTextEn: With reference to the special address of the President of India, which of the following/statements is/are correct? 1. The President addresses the joint meeting of both houses of Parliament at the commencements of the ﬁ rst session after each general election of the house of the people and at the commencement of the ﬁ rst session of each year. 2. The President in his address informs the Parliament of the causes of its summons. Select the correct answer using the codes given below. Codes:
questions.questionTextHi: भारत के राष्ट्रपति के विशेष संबोधन के संदर्भ में, निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा/से कथन सही है/हैं? 1. राष्ट्रपति लोक सभा के प्रत्येक आम चुनाव के बाद पहले सत्र की शुरुआत पर और प्रत्येक वर्ष के पहले सत्र की शुरुआत पर संसद के दोनों सदनों की संयुक्त बैठक को संबोधित करते हैं। 2. राष्ट्रपति अपने अभिभाषण में संसद को उसके आह्वान के कारणों की जानकारी देते हैं। नीचे दिए गए कोड का उपयोग करके सही उत्तर चुनें। कोड:
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (C). All executive power is vested in the President of India. The Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister aids and advises the President who exercises his powers in accordance to such advice. Article 87 of the constitution provides two instances when the President specially addresses both Houses of Parliament. The President of India addresses both the Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha at the beginning of the ﬁrst Session after each general election when the reconstituted lower house meets for the ﬁrst time. The President also addresses both the houses at beginning of the ﬁrst session of each year. The President's speech essentially highlights the government's policy priorities and plans for the upcoming year. The address provides a broad framework of the government's agenda and direction.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following expression is appropriate regarding the message to call joint sitting of both houses under Article 108 of the Constitution of India?
questions.questionTextHi: भारत के संविधान के अनुच्छेद 108 के अंतर्गत दोनों सदनों की संयुक्त बैठक बुलाने के संदेश के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी अभिव्यक्ति उपयुक्त है?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). Article 108-Joint sitting of the both Houses in certain cases- If after a Bill has been passed by one House and transmitted to the other House — (a) the Bill is rejected by the other House; or (b) the Houses have ﬁnally disagreed as to the amendments to be made in the Bill; or (c) more than six months elapse from the date of the reception of the Bill by the other House without the Bill being passed by it, the President may, unless the Bill has elapsed by reason of a dissolution of the House of the People, notify to the Houses by message if they are sitting or by public notiﬁcation if they are not sitting, his intention to summon them to meet in a joint sitting for the purpose of deliberating and voting on the Bill. Hence option (a) is correct.

Hence option (a) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: What will be happened if President summons for the joint session of Parliament and in the meantime Lok Sabha dissolved?
questions.questionTextHi: यदि राष्ट्रपति संसद का संयुक्त सत्र बुलाएँ और इसी बीच लोकसभा भंग हो जाए तो क्या होगा?
optionsEn: Joint session will be held in scheduled time
Joint session will be held after composition of New Lok Sabha
optionsHi: संयुक्त सत्र निर्धारित समय पर आयोजित किया जाएगा
संयुक्त सत्र रद्द कर दिया जाएगा
नई लोकसभा के गठन के बाद संयुक्त सत्र आयोजित किया जाएगा
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). The President can summon both the Houses to meet in a joint sitting for the purpose of deliberating & voting on the bill. If the bill (under dispute) has already lapsed due to the dissolution of the Loksabha, no joint sitting can be summoned. But the joint sitting can be held if the Lok Sabha is dissolved after the President has notiﬁ ed his intentions to summon such a sitting (as the bill does not lapse in this case). So option (a) is correct.

But the joint sitting can be held if the Lok Sabha is dissolved after the President has notiﬁ ed his intentions to summon such a sitting (as the bill does not lapse in this case). So option (a) is correct.

A private member's bill is a bill presented by a Member of Parliament who is not elected but only nominated by the President of India. 2. Recently, a private member's bill has been passed in the Parliament of India for the ﬁ rst time in its history. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.questionTextHi: भारत की संसद के संदर्भ में, निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें: 1. एक निजी सदस्य का विधेयक एक संसद सदस्य द्वारा प्रस्तुत किया गया विधेयक है जो निर्वाचित नहीं होता है बल्कि केवल भारत के राष्ट्रपति द्वारा नामित होता है। 2. हाल ही में, भारत की संसद में इतिहास में पहली बार एक निजी विधेयक पारित किया गया है। ऊपर दिए गए कथनों में से कौन सा/से सही है/हैं?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (D). A private member's Bill is a Bill presented by any member other than a Minister. The diﬀ erence in two cases is that any member other than a Minister desiring to introduce a Bill has to give a notice of his intention and to ask for leave of the House to introduce the Bill. If a Bill has been published in the oﬃ cial gazette before it's introduction, no motion for leave to introduce the Bill is necessary. About a dozen of private Bills have been passed since the independence. Thus, neither statement 1 nor statement 2 is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. A Bill pending in the Lok Sabha lapses on its prorogation. 2. A Bill pending in the Rajya Sabha, which has not been passed by the Lok Sabha, shall not lapse on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.questionTextHi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा/से कथन सही है/हैं? 1. लोकसभा में लंबित एक विधेयक अपने सत्रावसान पर समाप्त हो जाता है। 2. राज्यसभा में लंबित कोई विधेयक, जो लोकसभा द्वारा पारित नहीं किया गया है, लोकसभा के विघटन पर समाप्त नहीं होगा। नीचे दिए गए कोड का उपयोग करके सही उत्तर चुनें:
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (B). According to Article 107(3) of the Indian Constitution, a Bill pending in Parliament shall not lapse by reason of prorogation of the House. So, statement (1) is not correct. Article 107(4) of the Indian Constitution states that a Bill pending in the Council of States which has not been passed by the House of People shall not lapse on the dissolution of the House of People. Thus, statement (2) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Consider the following statements: 1. The Chairman and the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha are not the members of that House. 2. While the nominated members of the Both Houses of the Parliament have no voting right in the Presidential election, they have Right to Vote in the election of the Vice-President. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.questionTextHi: निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें: 1. राज्य सभा के सभापति और उपसभापति उस सदन के सदस्य नहीं होते हैं। 2. जबकि संसद के दोनों सदनों के नामांकित सदस्यों को राष्ट्रपति चुनाव में मतदान का कोई अधिकार नहीं है, उन्हें उपराष्ट्रपति के चुनाव में मतदान का अधिकार है। ऊपर दिए गए कथनों में से कौन सा/से सही है/हैं?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (B). Statement 1 is incorrect. The Chairman of Rajya Sabha is the Vice-President. However, the Deputy Chairman is a member of the Rajya Sabha and is elected from amongst them. Statement 2 is correct. The electoral college in the Presidential election consists of the elected Members of the Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies. The Vice- Presidential election however as a part of its electoral college consist of all the members of the Parliament, whether elected or nominated.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (B) Statement 1 is incorrect. The Chairman of Rajya Sabha is the Vice-President. However, the Deputy Chairman is a member of the Rajya Sabha and is elected from amongst them. Statement 2 is correct. The electoral college in the Presidential election consists of the elected Members of the Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies. The Vice- Presidential election however as a part of its electoral college consist of all the members of the Parliament, whether elected or nominated.

questions.questionTextEn: Who has the right to issue money from the Consolidated Fund of India?
questions.questionTextHi: भारत की संचित निधि से धन जारी करने का अधिकार किसे है?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (D). According to Article 266 of the Indian Constitution, all revenues received by the Government of India, all loans raised by that Government by the issue of treasury bills, loans or ways and means, advances and all money received by that Government in the repayment of loans shall form one Consolidated Fund of India. It is under the control of Parliament. No amount can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund without the authorization from the Parliament. So the authority to issue money according to the Budgetary provisions from the Consolidated Fund can only be obtained if the Parliament permits it according to appropriation under Article 114.

It is under the control of Parliament. No amount can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund without the authorization from the Parliament. So the authority to issue money according to the Budgetary provisions from the Consolidated Fund can only be obtained if the Parliament permits it according to appropriation under Article 114.

questions.questionTextEn: With reference to the Union Government, consider the following statements: 1. The Department of Revenue is responsible for the preparation of Union Budget that is presented to the Parliament. 2. No amount can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India without the authorization from the Parliament of India. 3. All the disbursements made from Public Account also need the authorization from the Parliament of India. Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
questions.questionTextHi: केंद्र सरकार के संदर्भ में, निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें: 1. राजस्व विभाग संसद में प्रस्तुत किए जाने वाले केंद्रीय बजट की तैयारी के लिए जिम्मेदार है। 2. भारत की संसद की अनुमति के बिना भारत की संचित निधि से कोई भी राशि नहीं निकाली जा सकती। 3. सार्वजनिक खाते से किए गए सभी संवितरणों के लिए भी भारत की संसद से प्राधिकरण की आवश्यकता होती है। ऊपर दिए गए कथनों में से कौन सा/से सही है/हैं?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (C). The Ministry of Finance is responsible for the preparation of Union Budget which is presented to the Parliament. Therefore statement 1 is incorrect. No amount can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India without the authorization of the Parliament of India as provided in Article 114(3) of the Constitution. Thus, statement 2 is correct. The disbursement made from public account does not require authorization of Parliament of India. The control of this account is in the hands of the Executive. Thus statement 3 is also incorrect.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (C) The Ministry of Finance is responsible for the preparation of Union Budget which is presented to the Parliament. Therefore statement 1 is incorrect. No amount can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India without the authorization of the Parliament of India as provided in Article 114(3) of the Constitution. Thus, statement 2 is correct. The disbursement made from public account does not require authorization of Parliament of India. The control of this account is in the hands of the Executive. Thus statement 3 is also incorrect.

questions.questionTextHi: राष्ट्रपति आकस्मिकता निधि से कैसे खर्च कर सकते हैं?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (C). The Contingency Fund of India is established by Parliament by law under Article 267(1) of the Indian Constitution. This fund is placed at the disposal of the President of India, and no approval of the Parliament is needed while withdrawing the money from the fund. He may make advances out of this fund. It is to be used for the purpose of meeting unforeseen expenditures.

questions.questionTextHi: धन विधेयक को कौन प्रमाणित करता है?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (C). If any question arises whether a bill is a money bill or not, the decision of the Speaker of the Loksabha is ﬁ nal. questions.questionTextHi: धन विधेयक के बारे में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सही नहीं है?
optionsEn: A Money Bill can be tabled in either House of Parliament
The Speaker of Lok Sabha is the ﬁ nal authority to decide whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not
The Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill passed by the Lok Sabha and send it for consideration within 14 days
The President can not return a Money Bill to the Lok Sabha for reconsideration
optionsHi: धन विधेयक संसद के किसी भी सदन में पेश किया जा सकता है
लोकसभा अध्यक्ष यह तय करने का अंतिम प्राधिकारी है कि कोई विधेयक धन विधेयक है या नहीं
राज्यसभा को लोकसभा द्वारा पारित धन विधेयक को 14 दिनों के भीतर वापस करना होगा और विचार के लिए भेजना होगा
राष्ट्रपति किसी धन विधेयक को पुनर्विचार के लिए लोकसभा को नहीं लौटा सकता
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). A Money Bill can be introduced in Lok Sabha only. Rajya Sabha has got very limited power in this regard. Rajya Sabha can delay this for a period not exceeding 14 days.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (A) A Money Bill can be introduced in Lok Sabha only. Rajya Sabha has got very limited power in this regard. Rajya Sabha can delay this for a period not exceeding 14 days.

questions.questionTextEn: Of the following statements, which one is not correct?
questions.questionTextHi: निम्नलिखित कथनों में से कौन सा सही नहीं है?
optionsEn: The Rajya Sabha is powerless in money matters.
Money Bill is introduced in the Rajya Sabha.
The Rajya Sabha has to pass the Money Bill within 14 days after it has been passed by the Lok Sabha.
The Rajya Sabha may pass or return the Money Bill with some recommendations to the Lok Sabha.
optionsHi: धन के मामले में राज्यसभा शक्तिहीन है।
धन विधेयक राज्यसभा में पेश किया जाता है।
लोकसभा से पारित होने के बाद राज्य सभा को धन विधेयक को 14 दिनों के भीतर पारित करना होता है।
राज्य सभा धन विधेयक को कुछ सिफ़ारिशों के साथ पारित कर सकती है या लोकसभा को लौटा सकती है।
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (B). It has been laid down in Article 109 (1) of the Constitution of India that a Money Bill shall not be introduced in the Rajya Sabha. Article 109(2) lays down that, after a Bill has been passed by the Lok Sabha, it shall be transferred to the Rajya Sabha for its recommendations. In turn, the Rajya Sabha, within a period of 14 days of its receipt of the Bill, shall return the Bill with or without its recommendation to the Lok Sabha, which may accept or reject all or any of the recommendations of the Rajya Sabha.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (B) It has been laid down in Article 109 (1) of the Constitution of India that a Money Bill shall not be introduced in the Rajya Sabha. questions.questionTextHi: भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 110 के तहत धन विधेयक की परिभाषा क्या है?
optionsEn: The imposition, abolition, alteration or regulation of any tax
The regulation of borrowings of money
The appropriation of money out of the consolidated fund of India
Declaration of any expenditure to be charged on the consolidated fund of India (e) None of the above / More than one of the above
optionsHi: किसी कर का अधिरोपण, उन्मूलन, परिवर्तन या विनियमन
भारत की संचित निधि से धन का विनियोग
भारत की समेकित निधि पर लगाए जाने वाले किसी भी व्यय की घोषणा (ई) उपरोक्त में से कोई नहीं / उपरोक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (E). According to the Article 110 of the Constitution of India, a Bill shall be deemed to be a money bill if it contains only provisions dealing with all or any of the following matters, namely: (a) The imposition abolition, remission, alteration or regulation of any tax, (b) The regulation of borrowings of money or the giving of any guarantee by the GOI. (c) The appropriation of money out of the consolidated fund of India. (d) The declaration of any expenditure to the expenditure charged on the consolidated fund of India or the increasing of the amount of any such expenditure. Thus all the options are correct. So the correct answer is an option (e).

optionsEn: A bill shall be deemed to be a Money Bill if it contains only provisions relating to imposition, abolition, remission, alteration or regulation of any tax.
A Money Bill has provisions for the custody of the Consolidated Fund of India or the Contingency Fund of India.
A Money Bill is concerned with the appropriation of moneys out of the Contingency Fund of India.
A Money Bill deals with the regulation of borrowing of money or giving of any guarantee by the Government of India.
optionsHi: किसी विधेयक को धन विधेयक माना जाएगा यदि उसमें केवल किसी कर को लगाने, समाप्त करने, छूट देने, परिवर्तन या विनियमन से संबंधित प्रावधान हों।

Thus it is operated by the executive action and not by Legislative Procedure into which money bills (Art. 110) are placed.

questions.questionTextEn: In India, which of the following review the independent regulators in sectors like telecommunications, insur- ance, electricity, etc.? 1. Ad Hoc Committees set up by the Parliament 2. Parliamentary Department Related Standing Committees 3. Finance Commission 4. Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission 5. NITI Aayog Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.questionTextHi: भारत में निम्नलिखित में से कौन दूरसंचार, बीमा, बिजली आदि क्षेत्रों में स्वतंत्र नियामकों की समीक्षा करता है? 1. संसद द्वारा गठित तदर्थ समितियाँ 2. संसदीय विभाग संबंधित स्थायी समितियाँ 3. वित्त आयोग 4. वित्तीय क्षेत्र विधायी सुधार आयोग 5. नीति आयोग नीचे दिए गए कोड का उपयोग करके सही उत्तर चुनें।
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). In India, there are 24 departments related standing committees that comprise members from both houses of parliament. These committees one ministry speciﬁ c, & may review the working of regulators within their respective department. Parliament may also establish ad-hoc committees which may examine the working of regulators. eg. Joint parliamentary committee on the allocation of 2G spectrum includes the review of the policy on spectrum pricing & grant of telecom licenses ad-hoc committees are temporary in nature. Finance commission, NITI Aayog & Financial sector legislative reforms commission has no role to play in review of Independent regulators in various sectors.

questions.questionTextEn: ‘Votes on Account’ permits Union Government to:
questions.questionTextHi: 'लेखानुदान' केंद्र सरकार को इसकी अनुमति देता है:
optionsEn: Borrow money from the Reserve Bank of India
Withdraw money from the Consolidated Fund of India for speciﬁ c period
optionsHi: भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक से पैसा उधार लें
विशिष्ट अवधि के लिए भारत की संचित निधि से धन निकालना
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (D). Article 116 of the Indian Constitution states that in case the Appropriation Bill is not passed and the Union government requires withdrawal of money, it can through Vote on Account have the power to authorize by law the withdrawal of money from the Consolidated Fund of India.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (D) Article 116 of the Indian Constitution states that in case the Appropriation Bill is not passed and the Union government requires withdrawal of money, it can through Vote on Account have the power to authorize by law the withdrawal of money from the Consolidated Fund of India.

questions.questionTextEn: Vote on Account is meant for
questions.questionTextHi: लेखानुदान का मतलब है
optionsEn: Vote on the report of CAG
Appropriating funds pending passing of budget
Budget (e) None of the above/More than one of the above
optionsHi: CAG की रिपोर्ट पर वोट करें
अप्रत्याशित व्यय को पूरा करने के लिए
बजट पारित होने तक धनराशि का विनियोजन
बजट (ई) उपरोक्त में से कोई नहीं/उपरोक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (C). Vote on-Account is presented when Government has no time to present full Budget or elections are around the corner. When the Government does not have enough time to vote for a full budget before the commencement of the new ﬁ nancial year, a special provision is made to make sure that there is enough money at the disposal of the Government to allow it to run the administration of the country. This special provision is known as Vote-on-Account. Article 116(1)(a) of the Constitution has provision of vote-on-Account.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (C) Vote on-Account is presented when Government has no time to present full Budget or elections are around the corner. When the Government does not have enough time to vote for a full budget before the commencement of the new ﬁ nancial year, a special provision is made to make sure that there is enough money at the disposal of the Government to allow it to run the administration of the country. This special provision is known as Vote-on-Account. Article 116(1)(a) of the Constitution has provision of vote-on-Account.

questions.questionTextEn: What is the diﬀ erence between ‘Vote-on-Account’ and ‘interim budget’? 1. The provision of a ‘Vote-on-Account’ is used by a stable Government, while ‘interim budget’ is a provision used by a caretaker Government. 2. A ‘Vote-on-Account’ only deals with the expenditure in Government’s budget while an ‘interim budget’ includes both expenditure and receipts. Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
questions.questionTextHi: 'लेखानुदान' और 'अंतरिम बजट' के बीच क्या अंतर है? 1. 'लेखानुदान' का प्रावधान एक स्थिर सरकार द्वारा उपयोग किया जाता है, जबकि 'अंतरिम बजट' एक कार्यवाहक सरकार द्वारा उपयोग किया जाने वाला प्रावधान है। 2. 'लेखानुदान' केवल सरकार के बजट में होने वाले व्यय से संबंधित होता है जबकि 'अंतरिम बजट' में व्यय और प्राप्तियां दोनों शामिल होते हैं। ऊपर दिए गए कथनों में से कौन सा/से सही है/हैं?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (B). A Vote-on-Account is the expenditure outlay for the functioning of the government presented by the Finance Minister to the Parliament seeking approval for the estimated expenses to be incurred in the next few months. While vote- on-account is sometimes referred to as Interim Budget. Interim Budget is more than presenting the expenditure; it also provides the receipt estimates along with the estimated expenditure.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (B) A Vote-on-Account is the expenditure outlay for the functioning of the government presented by the Finance Minister to the Parliament seeking approval for the estimated expenses to be incurred in the next few months. While vote- on-account is sometimes referred to as Interim Budget. Interim Budget is more than presenting the expenditure; it also provides the receipt estimates along with the estimated expenditure.

questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding submission of Money bill?
questions.questionTextHi: धन विधेयक प्रस्तुत करने के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सही है?
optionsEn: The Finance Bill is presented in Rajya Sabha.
It can be presented in either House of Parliament.
It cannot be presented in Lok Sabha.
It is presented in Lok Sabha.
optionsHi: वित्त विधेयक राज्यसभा में पेश किया गया है.
इसे संसद के किसी भी सदन में प्रस्तुत किया जा सकता है।
इसे लोकसभा में पेश नहीं किया जा सकता.
इसे लोकसभा में पेश किया गया है.
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (D). The UPPSC has used the term Finance Bill in its Hindi version question paper, however English version question paper has the term Money Bill. So in this question, commission’s intention is Money Bill not the Finance Bill. Special procedure has been adopted in respect of Money Bills in Article 109 of the Constitution. Article 109 (1) states that the Money Bill cannot be presented in Rajya Sabha. So Money Bill is only presented in Lok Sabha.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (D) The UPPSC has used the term Finance Bill in its Hindi version question paper, however English version question paper has the term Money Bill. So in this question, commission’s intention is Money Bill not the Finance Bill. Special procedure has been adopted in respect of Money Bills in Article 109 of the Constitution. Article 109 (1) states that the Money Bill cannot be presented in Rajya Sabha. So Money Bill is only presented in Lok Sabha.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following proposals is related to the Union Budget?
questions.questionTextHi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा प्रस्ताव केंद्रीय बजट से संबंधित है?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (C). Censure Motion: Censure means the expression of strong disapproval or harsh criticism. It is generally against the policies of the Government. Calling Attention : With the prior permission of the Speaker, a member may call the attention of a Minister to any matter of urgent public importance and the Minister may make a brief statement or ask for time to make a statement at a later hour or date. Cut Motion : Cut motion is a power given to the member of the Lok Sabha to oppose a demand in the Financial Bill discussed by the Government. If a cut motion is adopted by the House and the Government does not have the numbers, it is obliged to resign. However the Lok Sabha has the right to permit the grant after reducing the amount, and they do so by cut motion which are of three types-token cut, policy cut, and frugality cut. Adjournment Motion: It is a motion to draw the attention of members of the House on a subject or matter of public importance.

questions.questionTextEn: What is meaning of Guillotine in Parliamentary Procedure?
questions.questionTextHi: संसदीय प्रक्रिया में गिलोटिन का क्या अर्थ है?
optionsEn: To stop the debate on the bill
To continue the debate on the bill
To adjourn the house (e) To adjourn the house for the day
optionsHi: बिल पर बहस रोकने के लिए
ताकि बिल पर बहस जारी रहे
सदन को स्थगित करना (ई) सदन को दिन भर के लिए स्थगित करना
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). Closure Motion - it is a motion moved by a member to cut short the debate on a matter before the House. There are four kinds of Closure Motions Guillotine in one of them. In Guillotine the undiscussed clauses of a bill or a resolution are also put to vote along with the discussed ones due to want of time (as the time allotted for the discussion is over)

optionsEn: Planning Commission is accountable to Parliament
President can make ordinance only when either of the two Houses of Parliament is not in session
The minimum age prescribed for appointment as a Judge of the Supreme Court is 40 years
National development Council is constituted of Union Finance Minister and the Chief Ministers of all the States
optionsHi: योजना आयोग संसद के प्रति जवाबदेह है
राष्ट्रपति तभी अध्यादेश जारी कर सकता है जब संसद के दोनों सदनों में से कोई भी सत्र नहीं चल रहा हो

Thus option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question_hi: भारतीय राजव्यवस्था के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सही है?
options_en: Planning Commission is accountable to Parliament
President can make ordinance only when either of the two Houses of Parliament is not in session
The minimum age prescribed for appointment as a Judge of the Supreme Court is 40 years
National development Council is constituted of Union Finance Minister and the Chief Ministers of all the States
options_hi: योजना आयोग संसद के प्रति जवाबदेह है
राष्ट्रपति तभी अध्यादेश जारी कर सकता है जब संसद के दोनों सदनों में से कोई भी सत्र नहीं चल रहा हो
सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के न्यायाधीश के रूप में नियुक्ति के लिए निर्धारित न्यूनतम आयु 40 वर्ष है
राष्ट्रीय विकास परिषद का गठन केंद्रीय वित्त मंत्री और सभी राज्यों के मुख्यमंत्रियों से होता है
questions.explanation_en: Correct Answer: (B). National Development Council is presided over by the prime minister of India. Thus it can not be constituted without the prime minister. Hence, option (d) is wrong. Under Article 123 of the constitution if at any time, except when both houses of parliament are in session, the president is satisﬁ ed that circumstances exist which render it necessary for him to take immediate action, he may promulgate such ordinances as the circumstances appear to him to require. Thus option (b) is the correct answer.

Thus option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.questionTextEn: Examine the following statements and choose the correct answer from the given options- 1. Right to Property is not a Fundamental Right now. 2. Rajya Sabha can stop a Financial Bill. 3. In the Preamble of Indian Constitution Secular and Democratic words were added by 42nd amendment of the Indian Constitution. 4. Any dispute of the Parliament can be resolved by the system of Speaker of the Lok Sabha. Code :
questions.questionTextHi: निम्नलिखित कथनों का परीक्षण करें और दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनें- 1. संपत्ति का अधिकार अभी मौलिक अधिकार नहीं है। 2. राज्यसभा किसी वित्तीय विधेयक को रोक सकती है। 3. भारतीय संविधान की प्रस्तावना में धर्मनिरपेक्ष और लोकतांत्रिक शब्द भारतीय संविधान के 42वें संशोधन द्वारा जोड़े गए। 4. संसद के किसी भी विवाद का समाधान लोकसभा अध्यक्ष की व्यवस्था द्वारा किया जा सकता है। कोड :
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). If the Finance Bill is not a Money Bill, Rajya Sabha can hold it like an ordinary Bill. However if the Finance Bill is a Money Bill, Rajya Sabha can stop it for 14 days only. Thus Rajya Sabha can stop the Financial Bill. By the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 of the Constitution, the characterization of India as ‘Sovereign Democratic Republic’ in the Preamble was changed to ‘Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic.’ The word ‘Unity of the Nation’ was replaced by ‘Unity and Integrity of the Nation’ in The Preamble. Statement (3) is wrong. In the case of any disagreement in both the Houses of the Parliament, there is a provision of Joint Session. However, there is no such provision made under which dispute of the Parliament can be resolved by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. By 44th Amendment Act 1978, the Right to Property, ceased to be a fundamental right and became a legal right(Article 300A). Thus, option (a) is the correct answer.

Statement (3) is wrong. In the case of any disagreement in both the Houses of the Parliament, there is a provision of Joint Session. questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following is the largest Committee of the Parliament?
questions.questionTextHi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी संसद की सबसे बड़ी समिति है?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (B). The work done by the Parliament in modern times is not only varied in nature but considerable in volume. The time at its disposal is limited. Hence it cannot give close consideration to all the legislative and other matters that come up before it. A good deal of its business is therefore transacted by what are called the Parliamentary Committees. The Committee on Public Accounts - The Committee consists of not more than 22 members comprising 15 members elected by Lok Sabha every year from amongst its members according to the principle of proportional representation by means of single transferable vote and not more than 7 members of Rajya Sabha nominated by that House are associated with the Committee. The examination of the Appropriation Accounts relating to the Railways, Defence Services, P&T Department and other Civil Ministries of the Government of India and reports of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India thereon as also the reports of the Comptroller and Auditor-General on revenue receipts mainly form the basis of the deliberation of the Committee. The tenure of this Committee is one year. The Committee on Estimates- The Estimates Committee, constituted for the ﬁ rst time in 1950, is a Parliamentary committee which consists of 30 Members, elected every year by the Lok Sabha amongst its members. The chairman of the committee is appointed by the Speaker amongst its members. The most important function of the committee is to suggest alternative policies to bring efficiency and economy in administration. The Committee on Public Undertakings - The Committee on Public Undertakings consist of 15 members elected by the Lok Sabha and 7 members of Rajya Sabha. A Minister is not eligible for election to this committee. The term of the committee is one year. The functions of the committee on public undertakings are : (a) To examine the reports and accounts of Public undertakings speciﬁ ed in the fourth Schedule to the Rules of Procedure and conduct of Business in Lok Sabha ; (b) To examine the reports, if any, of the comptroller and Auditor-General of India on the Public undertakings ; (c) To examine, in the context of the autonomy and eﬃ ciency of the Public undertakings whether the aﬀ airs of the Public undertakings are being managed in accordance with sound business principles and prudent commercial practices (d) To exercise such other Functions Vested in the Public Accounts Committee and Estimates committee in relation to the Public undertakings as are not covered by clauses (a), (b) and (c) above and as may be alloted to the committee by the speaker from time to time. The Committee on Petitions: - Committee on Petition in Lok Sabha consists of 15 members, while committee on petition in Rajya Sabha consists of 10 members. A minister is not nominated to this committee. The function of the committee is to consider and report on petitions presented to the House. Besides, it also considers representations from individuals and associations, etc. on subjects which are not covered by the rules relating to petitions and gives directions for their disposal.

questions.questionTextEn: With reference to the Parliament of India, which of the following Parliamentary Committees scrutinizes and reports to the House whether the powers to make regulations rules, sub-rules, by-laws, etc. conferred by the Constitution or delegated by the Parliament are being properly exercised by the Executive within the scope of such delegation?
questions.questionTextHi: भारत की संसद के संदर्भ में, निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी संसदीय समिति जांच करती है और सदन को रिपोर्ट करती है कि क्या संविधान द्वारा प्रदत्त या संसद द्वारा प्रत्यायोजित विनियम, नियम, उप-नियम, उप-कानून आदि बनाने की शक्तियों का कार्यपालिका द्वारा ऐसे प्रत्यायोजन के दायरे में उचित रूप से प्रयोग किया जा रहा है?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (B). *Parliament is too unwieldy a body to deliberate eﬀ ectively the issues that come up before it and the functions of Parliament are varied, complex & voluminous. questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following is not a tool of Parliamentary control over Public expenditures?
questions.questionTextHi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा सार्वजनिक व्यय पर संसदीय नियंत्रण का उपकरण नहीं है?
optionsEn: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
optionsHi: भारत के नियंत्रक एवं महालेखा परीक्षक

He has powers in relation to and of any other authority prescribed under any law made by Parliament. So CAG is not a tool of Parliamentary control over Public expenditure whereas rest options are under parliamentary control.

questions.questionTextEn: The members of Standing Committee of Parliament are taken from the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha in which ratio?
questions.questionTextHi: संसद की स्थायी समिति के सदस्य लोकसभा और राज्यसभा से किस अनुपात में लिये जाते हैं?
optionsEn: In equal numbers from both the Houses.
optionsHi: दोनों सदनों से बराबर संख्या में.
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). The Parliamentary Committees are of two kinds- Standing Committees and Ad-hoc Committees. Among the Standing Committees, there are three Financial Committees (1) Committees on Estimates, (2) Public Accounts, and (3) Public Undertakings. Excluding certain exceptional committees, the ratio of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha members in all other joint committees is approximately 2:1.

questions.questionTextEn: The Parliament of India exercises control over the functions of the Council of Ministers through 1. Adjournment motion 2. Question hour 3. Supplementary questions Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.questionTextHi: भारत की संसद 1. स्थगन प्रस्ताव 2. प्रश्नकाल 3. पूरक प्रश्नों के माध्यम से मंत्रिपरिषद के कार्यों पर नियंत्रण रखती है। नीचे दिए गए कोड का उपयोग करके सही उत्तर चुनें:
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (D). The Parliament of India exercises control over the functions of the council of Minister through' Adjournment Motion', 'Question Hour' and 'Supplementary Question'. This can be understood as: Adjournment Motion : The primary object of an adjournment motion is to draw the attention of the government to a matter of urgent public importance in respect of which a starred question, discussion of short duration or a resolution with requisite notice shall be too late. Question Hour is the ﬁ rst hour of every sitting of Parliament generally reserved for the asking and answering of questions. Question asked to a Minister are of three types- A starred Question (to which a member desires an oral answer in the House, supplementary questions can be asked thereon. Only 20 questions can be listed for oral answer on a day), An Unstarred Question (one which is not called for oral answer in the House and on which no supplementary questions can be asked) and A Short Notice Question (one which is related to matter of urgent public importance and can be asked with shorter notice than the period of notice prescribed for an ordinary question and followed by supplementary questions).

questions.questionTextEn: With reference to Union Government, consider the following statements: 1. The Ministries/Departments of the Government of India are created by the Prime Minister on the advice of the Cabinet Secretary. 2. Each of the Ministries is assigned to a Minister by the President of India on the advice of the Prime Minister. Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
questions.questionTextHi: केंद्र सरकार के संदर्भ में, निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें: 1. भारत सरकार के मंत्रालय/विभाग कैबिनेट सचिव की सलाह पर प्रधान मंत्री द्वारा बनाए जाते हैं। 2. प्रत्येक मंत्रालय को प्रधान मंत्री की सलाह पर भारत के राष्ट्रपति द्वारा एक मंत्री को सौंपा जाता है। ऊपर दिए गए कथनों में से कौन सा/से सही है/हैं?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (B). The Ministries/Departments of the Government of India are not created by Prime Minister on the recommendation of Cabinet Secretary. Cabinet Secretary is the head of Cabinet Secretariat. He is also the chairman of the Civil Services Board. Each of the Ministries is assigned to a Minister by the President of India on the advice of the Prime Minister. Hence, statement (1) is incorrect, and statement (2) is correct.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (B) The Ministries/Departments of the Government of India are not created by Prime Minister on the recommendation of Cabinet Secretary. Cabinet Secretary is the head of Cabinet Secretariat. He is also the chairman of the Civil Services Board. Each of the Ministries is assigned to a Minister by the President of India on the advice of the Prime Minister. Hence, statement (1) is incorrect, and statement (2) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Consider the following statements: 1. The Chairman of the Committee on Public Accounts is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. 2. The Committee on Public Accounts comprises Members of Lok Sabha, Members of Rajya Sabha and a few eminent persons of industry and trade. Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
questions.questionTextHi: निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें: 1. लोक लेखा समिति के अध्यक्ष की नियुक्ति लोकसभा अध्यक्ष द्वारा की जाती है। 2. लोक लेखा समिति में लोकसभा के सदस्य, राज्यसभा के सदस्य और उद्योग और व्यापार के कुछ प्रतिष्ठित व्यक्ति शामिल हैं। ऊपर दिए गए कथनों में से कौन सा/से सही है/हैं?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). The Lok Sabha appoints the chair persons of all Parliamentary committees. questions.questionTextHi: निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें: 1. जबकि राज्य सभा के सदस्य सार्वजनिक लेखा और सार्वजनिक उपक्रमों की समितियों से जुड़े होते हैं, अनुमान समिति के सदस्य पूरी तरह से लोकसभा से आते हैं 2. संसदीय संसदीय मंत्रालय संसदीय संसदीय समिति की कैबिनेट समिति के समग्र निर्देशन में काम करता है। 3. संसदीय एﬀ एयर मंत्री भारत सरकार द्वारा विभिन्न मंत्रालयों में गठित समितियों, परिषदों, बोर्डों और आयोगों आदि पर संसद सदस्यों को नामित करते हैं। इनमें से कौन सा कथन सही है?

questions.questionTextEn: Read the following statements related to Cabinet Committees and choose the correct option: Statement I : Cabinet Committees are not mentioned in the constitution. Statement II : Cabinet Committees are set up by the Prime Minister according to the exigencies of the time and requirements of the situation. Statement III : If Prime Minister is the member of Committee, he may not necessarily be the Chairman of Committee. Statement IV : Parliamentary Aﬀ airs Committee is chaired by the Prime Minister.
questions.questionTextHi: कैबिनेट समितियों से संबंधित निम्नलिखित कथनों को पढ़ें और सही विकल्प चुनें: कथन I: संविधान में कैबिनेट समितियों का उल्लेख नहीं है। कथन II: कैबिनेट समितियाँ समय की आवश्यकता और स्थिति की आवश्यकताओं के अनुसार प्रधान मंत्री द्वारा स्थापित की जाती हैं। कथन III: यदि प्रधान मंत्री समिति का सदस्य है, तो जरूरी नहीं कि वह समिति का अध्यक्ष हो। कथन IV: संसदीय एﬀ एयर समिति की अध्यक्षता प्रधान मंत्री करते हैं।
optionsEn: Statements I, II and III are true, but Statement IV is false.
Statements II, III and IV are true but Statement I is false.
Statements I and II are true, but Statement III and IV are false.
optionsHi: कथन I, II और III सत्य हैं, लेकिन कथन IV गलत है।
कथन II, III और IV सत्य हैं लेकिन कथन I गलत है।
कथन I और II सत्य हैं, लेकिन कथन III और IV गलत हैं।
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (D). Cabinet Committees are not mentioned in the Constitution. So they are extra - constitutional bodies. Rules of Business provides for their establishment. Thus, Statement I is true. Cabinet Committees are set up by the Prime minister ac- cording to the exigencies of the time and requirements of the situation. Thus, Statement II is true. Cabinet Committees are mostly Chaired by the Prime Minister. Some times other Cabinet Ministers, the Finance Minister or the Home Minister also acts as chairman but in case if Prime Minister is the member of Committee, he is necessarily the Chairman of the Committee. Thus, Statement III is false Cabinet Committee on Parliamentary Aﬀ airs is chaired by Minister of Defence, not by Prime Minister. Thus Statement IV is false.

questions.questionTextEn: The main function of the Public Accounts Committee of Parliament is-
questions.questionTextHi: संसद की लोक लेखा समिति का मुख्य कार्य है-
optionsEn: To examine the ﬁ nancial account of the government and report of Comptroller and Auditor General.
To appoint on higher posts of public sector units.
To examine the policy according to ﬁ nancial provision.
optionsHi: सरकार के वित्तीय खाते और नियंत्रक एवं महालेखा परीक्षक की रिपोर्ट की जांच करना।
सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र की इकाइयों के उच्च पदों पर नियुक्ति करना।
वित्तीय प्रावधान के अनुसार नीति का परीक्षण करना।
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). The Public Accounts Committee is a Parliamentary committee that controls public expenditure. The function of this committee is to examine the report of accounts of the Union Government submitted by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India and to lay this report before each House of the Parliament. Its aim is to highlight the misuse and misappropriation of public expenditure before each House of the Parliament. It also recommends action against those public authorities who are found responsible for the misuse of the expenses. It also counterchecks the public expenditure on the basis of the report of Comptroller and Auditor General. The member of opposition of the Lok Sabha is appointed as the Chairman of this Committee (since 1967-68). The report of the Public Accounts Committee is submitted to the Speaker of Lok Sabha.

questions.questionTextEn: Consider the following statements The Parliamentary Committee on Public Accounts 1. consists of not more than 25 Members of the Lok Sabha. 2. scrutinizes appropriation and ﬁ nance accounts of the Government. 3. examines the report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.questionTextHi: निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें लोक लेखा पर संसदीय समिति 1. में लोकसभा के 25 से अधिक सदस्य नहीं होते हैं। 2. सरकार के विनियोग और वित्त खातों की जांच करता है। 3. भारत के नियंत्रक एवं महालेखा परीक्षक की रिपोर्ट की जाँच करता है। ऊपर दिए गए कथनों में से कौन सा/से सही है/हैं?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (B). Statement 1 is incorrect because the PAC consists of only 22 members, of which 15 are from Lok Sabha and 7 from Rajya Sabha. The PAC examines the report of the Comptroller and Auditor General, which also includes the examination of the appropriation and ﬁ nance accounts of the Government of India.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (B) Statement 1 is incorrect because the PAC consists of only 22 members, of which 15 are from Lok Sabha and 7 from Rajya Sabha. The PAC examines the report of the Comptroller and Auditor General, which also includes the examination of the appropriation and ﬁ nance accounts of the Government of India.

questions.questionTextEn: Who nominates the Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee of Indian Parliament?
questions.questionTextHi: भारतीय संसद की लोक लेखा समिति के अध्यक्ष को कौन नामांकित करता है?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). The chairman of the Public Accounts Committee is appointed by the Speaker from amongst its members. Till 1966-67, the chairman belonged to the ruling party. The committee consists of not more than 22 members comprising 15 members of Lok Sabha and not more than 7 members of Rajya Sabha. For the ﬁ rst time, the Speaker appointed a member of the opposition as the chairman of the committee during 1967-68. This practice has been continued since then. A minister is not eligible to be elected a member of the committee.

For the ﬁ rst time, the Speaker appointed a member of the opposition as the chairman of the committee during 1967-68. This practice has been continued since then. A minister is not eligible to be elected a member of the committee.
